title: MyRecon vs Recon-ng: OSINT Tools Compared
description: Compare MyRecon and Recon-ng: search inputs, public-source workflows and verification limits. Choose an OSINT tool for your authorized research.
h1: MyRecon vs Recon-ng: compare public-search workflows
intro: Looking for a Recon-ng alternative depends on the task: Recon-ng is described by its official source as an open-source modular reconnaissance framework. MyRecon is a browser route into a public username search. This page compares workflow and fit without inventing a speed score or claiming identical coverage.

sections.heading: What Recon-ng is designed to do
sections.body: Recon-ng is described by its official source as An open-source modular reconnaissance framework. Its published workflow is a configurable framework with modules and an analyst-managed workflow. Confirm current access, terms, and available features directly with the provider before relying on a capability for a live investigation.

sections.heading: Where a MyRecon username workflow fits
sections.body: MyRecon starts from a username and is intended to help review public profile leads across supported checks. Open every candidate source yourself: a handle match is not proof of identity, and unsupported, blocked, or unavailable checks should not be read as a confirmed absence.

sections.heading: Compare evidence rather than headline counts
sections.body: The tools can use different inputs, data sources, and result rules, so an unmeasured count or speed claim would not be a fair comparison. For Recon-ng, check the official documentation linked below; for either workflow, confirm the original source, date, and reason a result is relevant.

cta.label: Search a public username with MyRecon

faq.question: Is MyRecon a direct replacement for Recon-ng?
faq.answer: Not for every task. Recon-ng is documented as an open-source modular reconnaissance framework. MyRecon focuses on a browser-based public username workflow. Choose based on required inputs, access model, source coverage, and the current official documentation.

faq.question: Does MyRecon check more sites than Recon-ng?
faq.answer: No measured, same-scope benchmark is published here, so this page makes no coverage or speed superiority claim. Compare the current source lists, methods, and result definitions under the same authorized test conditions.

faq.question: Can either tool prove two profiles belong to one person?
faq.answer: A matching username alone cannot establish identity. Open the underlying public profiles and corroborate any proposed connection with independent, voluntarily published context; keep uncertain outcomes clearly labeled.
